unit.why: A biographical opening on R. Levi Yitzhak of Berditchev that contains a short birth anecdote: the Besht twice served his disciples drink and cake, saying a soul had come into the world that would advocate for Israel.
unit.boundary_note: biographical chapter on R. Levi Yitzhak continues into next division

stories.end_quote: עבור אחב"י אין די באר ואין די ספר
stories.summary_en: At the birth of R. Levi Yitzhak of Berditchev in 1740, the Besht twice gave his disciples drink and cake, announcing that a soul had come into the world that would plead in Israel's defence.

tags.why: The anecdote is about the birth of R. Levi Yitzhak, marked by the Besht.
His birth is the event of the anecdote.

quotes: נתן לתלמידיו משקה עם לייקיך ב' פעמים
tags.why: The Besht serves drink in celebration.

quotes: שאמר שבא לעולם נשמה שתמליץ טוב
tags.why: The Besht knows from afar that a great soul has been born.

quotes: ומפורסם לכל מליצותיו הטובות עבור אחב"י
tags.why: The Besht foretells the child's role as advocate for Israel, which the text says came true.

quotes: והי׳ תלמוד מובהק להגאון האלקי קוה"ק רבינו דוב בער
tags.why: His discipleship under the Maggid is stated, though only in passing.
